newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy 98 budget close to 28 trln lire - Pennacchi.
newsitem.headline: Italy 98 budget close to 28 trln lire - Pennacchi.

text.p: Italy needs to make deficit cuts of between 25 trillion and 28 trillion lire in its 1998 budget and the precise sum is likely to be at the high end of the scale, Treasury Ministry undersecretary Laura Pennacchi said on Tuesday.
She made the estimate in a speech to a seminar on the welfare state. Other government officials have previously spoken of a deficit-cutting budget of 25 trillion lire.
The extent of the deficit cuts will be stated in the centre-left government's document of three-year rolling economic targets (DPEF), which political sources say the cabinet could approve on Friday.

Pennacchi said the issue was how the deficit cuts should be achieved. "Either you challenge the figure of 25 to 28 trillion lire, which in reality is more like 28, or you talk about how to achieve it," Pennacchi said.
Leaders of political parties which support the government met Prime Minister Romano Prodi on Monday night to discuss the DPEF but failed to resolve differences over any welfare cuts in the measures.
Pennacchi said all the pro-government parties, including the hard-left Communist Refoundation party, agreed that the welfare state had to be reformed.
